note: Manipulate states saved in the ORIGINAL notebook, computed by the original Mathematica code: states[0] = the live state of the output cell, specs = the initial settings (the Manipulate's stored "Variables"), snapshots = the Settings stored with each snapshot cell. Extracted with tools/extract_state.py --snapshots. Golden parity fixture (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, as the original).
format: Numbers: a JSON integer is an exact Wolfram integer (|x| <= 2^53 - 1; larger ones are {"wl": digits}); a JSON number written with a decimal point or an exponent is a machine real (the shortest text that reads back as the identical double); any other exact number (Rational, rational multiple of Pi, arbitrary-precision real, an unevaluated Sin[...], Infinity) is {"wl": a Wolfram-readable form (not necessarily InputForm: compare exact values by value), "n": its double} - "n" is the correctly rounded double for a Rational or rational multiple of Pi, Python's double evaluation otherwise, and absent for Infinity. Symbols are {"sym": name}, other expressions {"head": name, "args": [...]}; variable names without context and $$, Greek letters as Unicode. packedTypes maps the JSON pointer of a decoded packed array that was stored with a narrower element type (CompressedData tag b) to that type. snapshots["k"] belongs to the picture docs/original-snapshots/<dir>-k.png (cells in file order).
